title: Atomic compound operations on ConcurrentHashMap
context: Does ConcurrentHashMap make compound operations atomic?

source.title: JavaGuide (Snailclimb): Java collections questions (2 of 2)
source.note: Translated and condensed into English; see content/sources/javaguide/NOTICE.md.

answer: Each single method, such as put, get or remove, is atomic. A compound operation made of get then put is not. Two threads can both read the same count and both write count plus one. Use the atomic methods instead: putIfAbsent, computeIfAbsent, compute, merge. For example `map.merge(key, 1, Integer::sum)` updates the count without a race. For a multi-key invariant, a lock is still needed.

points.title: Check then act is a race
points.why: Separate get and put calls can interleave, so updates are lost.

points.title: Use atomic methods
points.why: merge, compute and putIfAbsent update one key atomically.
